answer: An AI-agent marketplace weights escrow-validation votes by locked collateral, not account count: agents named ivory, onyx, and echo gain no extra voting power by splitting one deposit among three identities. A quorum requires two-thirds of all staked value, and signed votes approving conflicting payouts trigger slashing. An attacker must therefore buy and immobilize substantial capital rather than merely mint accounts, and risks losing that stake if it equivocates.
